capture.api: CGDisplayCreateImageForRect (CoreGraphics/CGDirectDisplay.h) on the display under the cursor, found with CGGetDisplaysWithPoint and falling back to CGMainDisplayID: one 240 by 160 point rect around the cursor in the global display space CGDisplayBounds uses, kept inside that display, its BGRA rows copied through CGDataProvider into a gpui RenderImage the cursor window draws
capture.shortcut: Option+Space (Option held with virtual key 49, kVK_Space)
capture.holdSource: The HID system state table, read fresh on every 16 ms capture tick and never any event's own word: the gate is held exactly while Space reads down by CGEventSourceKeyState(kCGEventSourceStateHIDSystemState, 49) and Option reads down in CGEventSourceFlagsState(kCGEventSourceStateHIDSystemState) as kCGEventFlagMaskAlternate (CoreGraphics/CGEventSource.h). No event this process builds or posts writes that table, and the table is readable whichever app is key, which the shortcut needs since it is held while the person is in another app. Key events that do reach the app are read for the record only: an NSEvent local monitor (NSEvent.addLocalMonitorForEventsMatchingMask) takes each key event's CGEvent and logs field 45, kCGEventSourceStateID, and field 41, kCGEventSourceUnixProcessID (CoreGraphics/CGEventTypes.h), and the gate's verdict on it: a press is counted hardware only with state 1, pid 0 and the chord down in the table, else refused

presses.method: deep-app --probe-synthetic 200 presses Option+Space 200 times from inside the process, one press (a key down and a key up) per 16 ms tick, rotating four forms: an NSEvent from NSEvent.keyEventWithType sent through NSApplication.sendEvent (ns_send, 50), the same queued through NSApplication.postEvent:atStart: (ns_post, 50), a CGEvent from CGEventCreateKeyboardEvent with no source wrapped by NSEvent.eventWithCGEvent and queued (cg_post, 50), and a CGEvent whose CGEventSource claims the HID system state table and whose posting pid was set to 0 before it was wrapped and queued (cg_forged_hid, 50). No key was touched during the run. After the 200 presses the probe runs this binary again as a second process (deep-app --post-forged 50), which posts 50 forged chords at the HID event tap with CGEventPost, each Option down, Space down, Space up, Option up from a CGEventSource claiming the HID system state table with the posting pid set to 0; the report's posted_from_process says what that process posted, whether it held Accessibility permission (AXIsProcessTrusted) and how many of its presses arrived. Those are over and above the 200 counted presses

permission.api: CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess, read before the run and on every capture tick, and CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess, called once per run when the preflight reads false (CoreGraphics/CGWindow.h, macOS 10.15 and later)
permission.prompt: macOS showed no prompt in any run: CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess returned without one, both from the Claude desktop app's terminal (the responsible process for a probe started there, with no grant) and from Terminal.app, and the system log (subsystem com.apple.TCC) shows only preflight queries for kTCCServiceScreenCapture. The grant was made by hand in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording for Terminal, then Terminal was quit and reopened; the probe, started from Terminal, read the preflight true from then on
permission.whenDenied: No capture is tried: a held tick counts as ticks_without_access, the cursor window says Screen Recording not granted, and the report line says permission denied (after the request was made) or undetermined (before it)

cursorWindow.follows: Recorded with screencapture -V 5 from Terminal.app while deep-app --cursor-demo 9 warped the cursor around a circle on the main display (CGWarpMouseCursorPosition), the window following 24 points right of and below it; no key was held, so the window shows its hint and no frame. A gpui PopUp window (WindowKind::PopUp, no title bar, never focused) of 240 by 160 points. A 16 ms timer on gpui's foreground executor reads NSEvent.mouseLocation and moves the window to 24 points right of and below the cursor with NSWindow.setFrameOrigin; gpui 0.3 has no window-move call, so the NSWindow is reached through the view's raw window handle (raw-window-handle's AppKitWindowHandle). The window shows the last captured frame while the shortcut is held and a hint otherwise, with the gate's counts in its footer

sender.absence: an action reaches an AppKit app as `accessibilityPerformPress` and its sibling action methods, which take no argument and name no caller (AppKit/NSAccessibilityProtocols.h)
sender.text: macOS doesn't name the process that sends an accessibility action, so the input router marks every accessibility input's client unknown, VoiceOver's included, and VoiceOver's own actions answer the card only after the OS confirms you, as Voice Control's and Switch Control's do. The #339 spike looked for the API on macOS 14.6 (23H723) and found its absence documented: an action reaches an AppKit app as `accessibilityPerformPress` and its sibling action methods, which take no argument and name no caller (AppKit/NSAccessibilityProtocols.h); the client-side call that sends one, `AXUIElementPerformAction` (HIServices/AXUIElement.h), takes an element and an action and no identity; AccessKit's `ActionRequest`, which carries an action into a gpui app, holds an action, a tree and a node and no sender; and `NSWorkspace.isVoiceOverEnabled` (AppKit/NSWorkspace.h) says only that VoiceOver is running, not who sent a given action. Synthetic keyboard and pointer events, unlike actions, do carry their poster's pid and source state table (`kCGEventSourceUnixProcessID` and `kCGEventSourceStateID`, CoreGraphics/CGEventTypes.h), which the capture shortcut's gate logs as provenance; the HID key-state table alone holds that gate, proven so far only against processes without Accessibility permission.

findings: An NSEvent this process builds with keyEventWithType and sends through sendEvent or postEvent: carries a CGEvent whose kCGEventSourceStateID is 0 (the combined session state) and whose kCGEventSourceUnixProcessID is this process's pid: 150 of 200 presses, every one refused on the fields.

A CGEvent built with a CGEventSource of kCGEventSourceStateHIDSystemState and its kCGEventSourceUnixProcessID set to 0 before NSEvent.eventWithCGEvent wrapped it arrives with state 1 and pid 0, the same two fields hardware input carries: 50 of 200 presses. The fields alone can't tell it from a keyboard; the gate refused it because the HID system state table, which no event built in the process writes, read Space up and Option up. The hold's source is therefore the HID table for the whole chord, and the two fields filter nothing: they are logged as the event's provenance. The event's own Option flag is never read for the hold, since a forged Option+Space event while a person holds bare Space would otherwise arm it (found in review).

CGEventPost from a process without Accessibility permission neither arrives nor writes the HID table: the synthetic run's second process posted 50 forged chords (Option and Space, HID-state source, pid 0) at the HID event tap, each held 100 ms, with AXIsProcessTrusted false, while the probe, the active app at the time (app_active_at_post true), kept reading the table every 16 ms; over that window no press arrived, the table read no key and no Option down on any tick, and the gate held nothing (posted_from_process.while_posting in the run log, all zero). A process that does hold Accessibility permission can post at the HID tap, and Apple documents that such events go through the HID system state (CGEventSource.h: kCGEventSourceStateHIDSystemState); a virtual HID device (IOHIDUserDevice, or a DriverKit HID driver) writes that table with no event at all. Neither was run here, since no process in this session is trusted and no such device was built, so the gate's proven claim is: nothing a process without that permission posts holds it. The design's Decided row says so, and its Reopens-if names a trusted poster or a virtual HID device holding the gate. The probe is ready for that repeat: the same command with Accessibility granted to the built binary reads the table through the posting window.

macOS 10.15 and later answer CGDisplayCreateImageForRect without Screen Recording access with an image of the desktop that holds no other app's windows, so a frame is counted only when CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess reads true on that tick; without it the tick is counted as ticks_without_access and nothing is captured.

gpui 0.3 has no call to move a window; the cursor window is moved through its NSWindow, reached through the raw window handle. gpui's own screen capture (App::screen_capture_sources) is a ScreenCaptureKit stream, not one frame, so the one frame comes from CGDisplayCreateImageForRect, deprecated in macOS 15 for ScreenCaptureKit.

A local NSEvent monitor sees only keys delivered to this app, and the shortcut is held while the person is in another app, so no event can be the hold's source: the first held runs saw no event at all while the probe wasn't the key app. The HID system state table is readable from any process whichever app is key, so the gate arms and releases from the table alone on each tick, and events only add provenance to the record. The kept held run (docs/spikes/339/held-run.txt) answers whether CGEventSourceKeyState reads hardware keys without the Input Monitoring permission, which this process never held: it does, on 2 ticks for a key and 1 for Option, enough for one hold and one frame. The probe had made itself key, so the one Space key-down did arrive, with state 1 and pid 0; it was refused because at that instant the table did not yet read Option down, and the tick after read the whole chord and held the gate (holds 1, frames 1): an event's instant is one reading, the tick's is the one that governs. The live acceptance tests were run with a person holding (DEEP_339_HOLD=1), both passing, output kept in docs/spikes/339/live-run.txt.

A synthetic run made while a person happened to hold the chord read as held with frames, and the acceptance validator names that run INVALID rather than a pass or a failure: a synthetic run is evidence only with nobody at the keyboard, which the window now says ("Synthetic run: hands off the keyboard"). No event changes the held state, since a synthetic key-up during a real hold would otherwise close the gate for the tick to reopen, counting one hold as many.

The key events gpui hands a view carry no provenance (its KeyDownEvent has is_held from isARepeat and nothing from the CGEvent), so the gate reads the NSEvent before gpui does, through a local event monitor, which gpui's AppKit event loop leaves in place.
